title: Opal and the Great Stuffy Land Wobble-Palooza
subtitle: Langston's Troll-O-Matic starts a giant day of games, surprises and a very wobbly party.
editorialNote: Complete original story supplied in full.

paragraphs: The day began with sunshine, sparkles, and a very suspicious noise coming from Langston’s bedroom.
Opal looked up from her breakfast.
Lolo, her soft gray sloth lovey, was sitting beside her. She tilted her head.
Then Langston shouted, “I MEANT TO DO THAT!”
She and Lolo hurried upstairs, where they found Langston standing in the middle of his room. He was wearing a blanket as a cape, a mixing bowl as a helmet, and two enormous socks over his hands.
Behind him was a contraption made of pillows, cardboard tubes, blankets, and what appeared to be an entire trampoline.
“That’s the exciting part. I haven’t quite figured that out yet.”
“Did you build a machine without knowing what it does?”
Langston climbed onto a little platform.
“Today, I shall demonstrate the greatest invention in Stuffy Land history!”
A trumpet played one very short note.
Then a pillow shot across the room, bounced off the ceiling, and landed directly on Langston’s head.
Just then, Axey bounced into the room.
And that was how the biggest, silliest adventure in Stuffy Land began.
The Troll-O-Matic 5000 was supposed to be a machine that could create fun.
Langston explained that it would make games, surprises, parties, and possibly snacks.
“What happens if you pull the blue lever?”
“DO NOT TOUCH THE BIG SHINY ONE.”
Axey slowly pulled his paw away.
Lolo noticed something on the side of the machine. A little dial was spinning, even though nobody had touched it.
“Langston,” she said gently, “I think your machine is already running.”
The machine made a tiny clicking noise.
And then it exploded into a shower of glitter.
A glowing message appeared in the air:
The machine answered with a trumpet blast.
TODAY, STUFFY LAND WILL EXPERIENCE THE GREATEST DAY OF GAMES, GIGGLES, AND GOOFY SURPRISES!
Lolo looked at the machine again.
“And perhaps we should find out what all the buttons do before we start.”
Within minutes, the entire Stuffy Land crew had gathered in the big meadow.
Coatl arrived first, his enormous turtle shell resting naturally on his back. The glowing buttons on his underside shimmered gently as he walked.
Finley and Stella, the two fluffy white doodle girls, came trotting beside him. Finley carried her detective notebook, while Stella happily wagged her tail.
Cherryberry arrived with the Aphmau kitty crew.
There was Cinny, the cinnamon-roll kitty, who immediately began organizing the snacks.
Turtle Kitty peeked out of her shell.
The Dragon Couple flew overhead: the completely purple boy dragon kitty and his dark-blue girl companion with her light-blue gem.
Aaron-y arrived in his black hoodie, his gray-and-black fur and red highlights giving him a very serious secret-agent appearance.
Caterpillar Kitty wiggled along behind him, every colorful body segment bouncing in a different direction.
Unique Pink brought a craft basket full of ribbons, glitter, and tiny decorations.
Frosted Kitty rolled in with a donut-themed grin.
Vanilla-y and Swirly arrived together, already arguing about dessert.
“Vanilla is the most elegant flavor,” Vanilla-y declared.
“Chocolate is the most powerful flavor,” Swirly replied.
Aphmau-y arrived and gave Aaron-y a friendly nudge.
Snow Cone Kitty brought a little frosty sparkle.
Water Kitty made a tiny splash in the meadow fountain.
Fire Kitty warmed the chilly morning air.
Poison Kitty carried a mysterious little bottle, which Opal immediately asked her to keep safely closed.
Snowy brought a collection of snowflakes.
Nebula Johnny floated in with his glowing moon shield.
C arrived with her pink fur, black paws and tail, and pretty bows.
Mermaid Kitty swam through a sparkling ribbon of water.
Spirit Kitty spun gently through the breeze.
Evil Queen Kitty arrived wearing her purple-and-silver tiara, looking as regal as ever.
Onion Ring Kitty was so tiny that Finley almost walked right past her. Finley quickly stopped and gave her a careful little sniff.
And, of course, Coatl was there to make sure everyone stayed safe.
Opal looked around at her friends.
Langston jumped onto a tree stump.
“ATTENTION, STUFFY LAND! THE WOBBLE-PALOOZA IS OFFICIALLY OPEN!”
He pulled a lever on a small remote.
“Thank you. Thank you. I accept snacks as payment.”
The first event was the Wobble-Walk Challenge.
The goal was simple: cross a wobbly bridge made of soft cushions, bouncing platforms, and giant inflatable mushrooms.
She carefully crossed the bridge, balancing with her arms out.
Lolo followed, moving slowly and steadily.
Axey took one look at the bridge and shouted:
He bounced onto the first mushroom.
He landed on the second mushroom.
And then he landed right inside a basket of soft balls.
Finley crossed next, carefully investigating each cushion before stepping on it. Stella followed with a happy little trot, wagging her tail the entire way.
Coatl crossed slowly and steadily. His shell made him wobble just a little, but he kept his balance.
Cinny took a little cinnamon-roll snack break halfway across.
Turtle Kitty rolled through a tunnel underneath the bridge.
Caterpillar Kitty wiggled across, bending around every obstacle.
Unique Pink decorated the bridge with little ribbons as she crossed.
Snow Cone Kitty skated across a frosty patch.
Water Kitty splashed over a little puddle.
Fire Kitty carefully warmed a slippery section.
Mermaid Kitty swam underneath the bridge.
Spirit Kitty spun over the top.
Nebula Johnny floated with his moon shield.
The Dragon Couple flew together, then landed side by side at the finish.
He rolled too far and bumped into Frosted Kitty.
Frosted Kitty spun around like a donut.
Aphmau-y laughed so hard she nearly fell over.
C danced her way across the bridge, her bows bouncing.
Vanilla-y and Swirly argued about which one had crossed first.
Poison Kitty tried to convince the judges that she had crossed twice.
Evil Queen Kitty demanded a royal bridge of her own.
“I’m afraid we only have one bridge.”
“Then I shall declare this bridge mine!”
Opal reached out and helped steady her.
Then she finished the course with a very dignified little hop.
Onion Ring Kitty reached the finish line last, but she had discovered a tiny shortcut through a hole in one of the mushrooms.
The second event was the Great Mystery of the Missing Giggle Button.
Langston proudly displayed the Troll-O-Matic’s control panel.
And one tiny button that said:
“Before the next event,” Langston announced, “we need to press the Giggle Button!”
Finley immediately opened her detective notebook.
There was a tiny trail of glitter leading away from the control panel.
The group followed the trail through the meadow, past the mushroom bridge, and around the fountain.
It led to a little wooden door.
The door was barely big enough for Onion Ring Kitty.
Inside was a tiny creature made of colorful buttons and ribbons.
It was holding the missing Giggle Button.
“Hello,” Opal said. “Did you take our button?”
“I’m Button-Bob. I found it on the ground.”
“I thought it was a special treasure. I wanted to keep it.”
“It’s important to our machine, but we can make you a special button of your own.”
Unique Pink immediately opened her craft basket.
She created a tiny sparkling button with a little smile painted on it.
Button-Bob handed over the Giggle Button.
Langston put it back in the machine.
Then the machine exploded with laughter.
The whole meadow shook with giggles.
Even Coatl’s shell buttons flashed in a happy rhythm.
Langston laughed so hard that his saucepan helmet fell off.
The third event was the Troll-O-Matic Talent Tornado.
The machine had a new idea.
It began projecting little glowing circles onto the grass.
Each circle displayed a different talent.
Opal stepped onto the stage and performed a cheerful dance with Lolo. Lolo added little graceful movements, and together they made the audience smile.
Axey demonstrated his explorer skills by finding a tiny hidden treasure beneath the stage.
Finley showed everyone how to solve a mystery using clues.
Stella performed a sweet little twirl and a perfect sit.
Coatl made his glowing shell buttons shine in a beautiful pattern.
Cinny balanced a cinnamon-roll treat on her head.
Turtle Kitty popped in and out of her shell.
The Dragon Couple flew in a beautiful circle.
Caterpillar Kitty did a colorful wiggle dance.
Unique Pink made a sparkling sculpture.
Frosted Kitty performed a donut spin.
Banana Splitty and Snow Cone Kitty performed a matching routine.
Fire Kitty created a glowing ring.
Nebula Johnny made a miniature moon appear.
C performed a bow-filled dance that made everyone clap along.
Mermaid Kitty swam through a sparkling water ribbon.
Spirit Kitty spun in a tiny tornado.
Vanilla-y and Swirly performed a dessert duet.
Poison Kitty did a mysterious pretend potion trick.
Evil Queen Kitty gave a dramatic royal speech.
Onion Ring Kitty performed a teeny-tiny dance.
He ate one while standing on one foot.
Then he ate one while wearing his saucepan helmet backward.
“THANK YOU. I HAVE BEEN TRAINING FOR YEARS.”
Then the Troll-O-Matic started making a strange noise.
The giant orange button began flashing.
“Did you build it to do that?”
FINAL EVENT ACTIVATED: THE GREAT WOBBLE STORM!
Suddenly, every object in the meadow began wobbling.
The cushions bounced into the air.
And the entire meadow began gently wobbling like a giant bowl of jelly!
He bounced from mushroom to mushroom.
Finley and Stella chased bouncing cushions.
The Dragon Couple flew in circles.
Nebula Johnny’s moon shield floated around like a giant glowing balloon.
Caterpillar Kitty wiggled so much that every colorful segment seemed to have its own dance.
The mushroom bridge was tipping sideways.
And the Troll-O-Matic was shaking so hard that its little legs were lifting off the ground.
“Langston!” Opal called. “We need to stop the machine!”
A tiny flag popped out that said:
“Let’s think about what the machine needs.”
Opal looked at the control panel.
The buttons were flashing in a pattern.
“Wait. The buttons are flashing in the same order as the events!”
“Cherryberry! Can you help me remember the order?”
“The obstacle course, the mystery, the talent show, and now the wobble storm.”
“Maybe we need to finish the events in the right order!”
“I’m surprised I didn’t think of it.”
Coatl stood beside the machine to steady it.
Finley and Stella found the loose wires underneath.
Axey climbed up to reach the top panel.
Unique Pink used her ribbons to secure a wobbly lever.
Aaron-y carefully examined the control panel.
Aphmau-y helped him read the tiny symbols.
Nebula Johnny used his moon shield to protect the group from flying cushions.
Water Kitty cooled the overheated parts.
Fire Kitty kept the little engine warm enough to run.
Snowy made a tiny snowflake marker for each button.
Spirit Kitty spun the flying confetti away.
Mermaid Kitty guided the water around the machine.
Turtle Kitty tucked herself safely inside her shell and rolled a loose screw over to Coatl.
The Dragon Couple flew above the machine, helping Axey see the top panel.
Vanilla-y and Swirly held two levers at the same time, even though they argued about who was doing the harder job.
Cookie, Banana Splitty, and Snow Cone Kitty helped carry little pieces of equipment.
Cinny organized everything into neat piles.
C danced to keep everyone’s spirits up.
Poison Kitty carefully identified a bottle of harmless machine lubricant.
Evil Queen Kitty used her royal voice to coordinate the crowd.
Onion Ring Kitty squeezed through a tiny gap and found the final missing switch.
Lolo stayed beside Opal, holding her paw.
Finley and Stella pushed the little switch.
Langston reached for the orange button.
“I think this is the first time my invention has actually needed everyone.”
“That’s because it’s a team invention now.”
A giant cloud of golden confetti burst into the sky.
And the Troll-O-Matic displayed one final message:
SUCCESS! YOU HAVE UNLOCKED THE GREATEST POWER IN STUFFY LAND: TEAMWORK!
Langston stood proudly beside his invention.
“I would like to thank myself for creating this incredible machine.”
“Your machine almost bounced the entire meadow into the sky.”
Langston looked around at the group.
“Fine. I would like to thank EVERYONE for helping me create this incredible machine.”
Then the machine beeped one last time.
Opal picked it up and read the message:
CONGRATULATIONS! YOU HAVE COMPLETED THE WOBBLE-PALOOZA! YOUR PRIZE IS ONE VERY SPECIAL SURPRISE!
Inside was a little golden key.
There was a tiny drawing of a door on it.
On the back were three words:
The ground beneath the meadow gave a tiny rumble.
A little door appeared in the grass.
It was round, purple, and covered in stars.
She placed the key in the lock.
Inside was a staircase leading down to a giant underground party room.
It had glowing disco balls, rainbow lights, soft trampolines, pillow mountains, and a snack table that seemed to stretch forever.
There was even a giant sign:
WELCOME TO THE SECRET STUFFY LAND PARTY PALACE!
“FIRST ONE TO THE SNACK TABLE WINS!”
Opal laughed and followed with Lolo.
The Dragon Couple flew through the sparkling ceiling.
Water Kitty made a fountain of bubbles.
Fire Kitty lit the disco floor.
Snowy created a little snowflake dance corner.
Nebula Johnny hung his moon shield above the stage like a glowing decoration.
Unique Pink started making party hats.
Frosted Kitty and Langston became the official donut-and-troll dance team.
Finley and Stella played in a mountain of soft balls.
Coatl settled near the entrance, watching everyone with a happy smile.
Vanilla-y and Swirly finally agreed on one thing:
The snack table needed more desserts.
Opal danced right in the middle of the room with Lolo, Axey, and all her friends.
The laughter echoed through the secret palace.
And Langston climbed onto the stage for one final announcement.
“ATTENTION, EVERYBODY! I HAVE A NEW IDEA!”
“THE NEXT WOBBLE-PALOOZA WILL HAVE TWO HUNDRED EVENTS!”
“AND I WILL BE THE HEAD JUDGE!”
“AND THE LOSER WILL ALSO RECEIVE ONE THOUSAND COOKIES!”
Opal looked around at all her friends: the kitties, the dogs, the dragons, the turtle, the axolotl, her brother, and her very special sloth lovey.
Then Langston accidentally stepped on the Troll-O-Matic’s remote.
BONUS EVENT: EVERYONE MUST DO THE TROLLY WIGGLE!
And before anyone could stop him, he started wiggling.
Even Coatl gave a very slow, very dignified little wiggle.
Opal laughed until her cheeks hurt.
And the party continued until every last friend was happily exhausted.
As the night ended, Opal climbed into bed with Lolo tucked beside her.
“Next time, I’m building a machine that makes breakfast.”
“Pancakes, waffles, cookies, and possibly a giant pancake trampoline.”
And somewhere downstairs, the Troll-O-Matic gave one final, tiny BOING.
